Welcome to my website!
I am a PhD candidate in Economics at the University of Nottingham.
My research interests cover quantitative and applied labour economics, with a particular focus on search and matching in the context of informal employment.
I have worked in several international institutions in macro-fiscal, macro-financial and social policy.

title: Research
text:
Wages, amenities and the value of formal employment: A structural approach for Mexico Paper



Abstract


Informal employment is high and persistent in low- and middle-income economies; however, evidence suggests that workers move between informal and formal jobs frequently. Using data for Mexico, I document that informal-to-formal transitions are more frequent than transitions in the opposite direction, that most occur within the same firm, and that these generate only modest immediate wage gains. I use a two-sector search model with on-the-job search to estimate workers’ willingness to pay for a formal job, which captures both the wage and the non-wage reasons to accept one. I decompose the willingness to pay into sector-specific amenities, employment stability, and future job opportunities, including formal offers from the current employer. At the median informal wage, high-skilled workers are willing to pay USD 40–45 per month for a formal job, below its social-security cost, while low-skilled workers are close to indifferent. I find that once the within-firm route is included, the value of remaining informal rises as workers wait for better future formal employment opportunities in the same firm.
